_note: The trace-encodings registry: the recognized capture encodings a device may name in a trace segment, the toolchain that produces each, the trace layers it can legitimately capture, and how that capture tool's OWN integrity is established. This is the 'trace of the trace': a trace attests the device's execution, but the tracer is itself software running on the device, so its integrity has to be accounted for too. The device-side analogue of the algorithms registry: algorithms name the deterministic transforms an EO value may be derived by; this names the capture toolchains a trace segment may be produced by. integrity says where the tracer's trust comes from: in_kernel (the tracer is part of the measured kernel/firmware, so its integrity is already covered by the platform's boot measurement, the strongest kind); open_source_userspace (auditable, reproducible-buildable, but its running integrity depends on the platform); signed_userspace (a signed capture binary whose hash is measured); vendor_runtime (a proprietary runtime trusted through the platform's vendor attestation). A device's recognized_encodings in the device-platforms manifest MUST all appear here; a trace segment naming an unregistered encoding, or naming a layer the encoding cannot produce, is rejected at the write gate.

encodings.title: Linux ftrace (function and event tracer)
encodings._note: The kernel's built-in tracer. Because it lives in the kernel, its code is covered by the same measured boot that attests the rest of the platform: the trace of this trace is the kernel measurement itself.

encodings.title: Linux eBPF raw event stream
encodings._note: eBPF programs run in-kernel under the verifier; the attached programs' bytecode can itself be hashed into the trace, so an auditor sees exactly what instrumentation produced the stream.

encodings.title: Zephyr Common Trace Format
encodings._note: The RTOS tracer for payload and instrument computers. Built into the Zephyr image, so its integrity rides on the firmware measurement the PSA/DICE attestation already covers.

encodings.title: ROS 2 rosbag2 recording
encodings._note: Records the actual messages on a robot's topics: what the sensors emitted and what the stack consumed. Open source and auditable, but a userspace recorder, so its running integrity depends on the platform measurement, not on the recorder alone.

encodings.title: Perfetto system trace (Android / Linux)
encodings._note: The Android and Linux system profiler; it multiplexes ftrace and userspace producers. Open source, but the traced daemon is userspace, so it is one measurement step weaker than pure in-kernel ftrace.

encodings.title: NVIDIA Nsight Systems trace
encodings._note: Captures on-device model execution: which kernels ran on the GPU over which input. A proprietary NVIDIA runtime, so its trust flows from NVIDIA's platform attestation rather than from source you can read; the inference layer it produces is the one a robot's perception stack rests on.

encodings.title: Apple os_signpost / os_log trace
encodings._note: Apple's signposting trace on iOS/macOS. Proprietary; trusted through the Secure Enclave attestation of the device. Included so the mobile family has a capture path, at the vendor-runtime assurance level.
